utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Yes, I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. General Talic, good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I can hear in a language I can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Joanna Korner and Ann Sutherland for the Prosecution. Ann Sutherland is not well today because she's temporarily playing the part of case manager in the absence of Ms. Gustin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, and good Monday to you. I'm John Ackerman, I'm with Tania Radosavljevic and Marela Maglov, who I'd like to introduce to the Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Good afternoon to you. Appearance for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, and Mr. President. Michel Pitron and Natasha Fauveau for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I must make a correction. I am -- Marela Maglov got married. Her name is Marela Jevtovic. And I keep forgetting that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, then very briefly before we go back to the witness and those in the public gallery are told that they can't watch anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is what I was telling the guard. You know, I mean -- it's a pity. I see so many students, I presume, here in the gallery. And very soon you will see curtains dropping right in front of your faces, and you won't be able to follow anything. You came in the wrong courtroom today. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first matter is this: Witness 7.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That caused so much trouble last week. The reality is clearly he can't be called. Mr. Koumjian, I know, will make an application today for release of the transcripts. But my clear understanding is that he has to return to his home the day after tomorrow, and therefore it's quite impossible to call him. The likelihood is we shall be making an application to tender his evidence under Rule 92 in full with no cross-examination, but that will be discussed at a later stage. But there is absolutely nothing else we can do about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Ms. Korner, and we've taken note of what you've just said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the other matter is simply this, and it was the query I raised last Friday about May the 17th. We do need to organise our witnesses, and I wonder whether Your Honour had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I tried to see Judge Schomburg this morning, but we just couldn't tie up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think it's so much Judge Schomburg as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. But in other words, since we are talking of Trial Chamber II, in any case, we are trying to make sure that there will be a standard -- we adopt the same standard measures. I mean, in other words, it's not ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there's a slight confusion. All I was asking was whether this Court will be sitting on May the 17th. Do you remember it appeared on the Court calender as not sitting. And Your Honour was going to make some inquiries --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We did, actually, make an inquiry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is a decision that has been taken that there will be no sittings - any Chamber - on May the 17th, for certain internal reasons that I don't think I am allowed to divulge.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that's why I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: However, there is a slight possibility that some Chambers may actually decide to sit. And this is what I -- I want to make sure of.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Well, Your Honour, may I say that it would assist from the point of view of trying to organise witnesses if when Your Honours made a decision, you could let us know as soon as -- possibly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Actually, I had thought that I would be in a position to tell you today.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I missed Judge Schomburg this morning. I had other things to do. And -- but you will certainly -- I will certainly let you know by tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm very grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If not today, then by the end of the sitting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can I confirm that we're sitting in the -- was it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. Tomorrow we are sitting at half past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we all got a message saying on Tuesday we were sitting in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, you had that correct too. There were two messages.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And we never got the correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I think I had told you that in the morning, we are --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The three of us are going to attend the plenary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that we will miss the plenary, then, in the afternoon to concentrate on the sitting. But the sitting will start at 1.30, instead of 2.15. And if we can start at 1.15, we will start at 1.15, we'll let you know. And hopefully we will finish by -- by quarter to 6.00 or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm grateful. Obviously I know we discussed it with you, and then after the Court rose we received a message -- you're sitting in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are right. Because I received it too. But it was corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It wasn't corrected to us, I'm afraid. It may have been corrected to other people. However, Your Honour, I'm grateful. So it's 1.15, 1.30 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One last thing, Ms. Korner. Now, that 7.35 will not be giving evidence this week, as planned for tomorrow, I hope that you have made the necessary adjustments to your schedule.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we don't waste any time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we -- subject to a few tidying up matters, which I need to discuss because effectively this witness completes the Banja Luka witness evidence. The witness who will start thereafter is 7.77. I have various documents relating -- in other words, a list of the documents. I know that Your Honour said that you've been given this overall rather confusing list, which I'm going to hand to Your Honours' legal officer at the break and discuss. But there are copies of everything for Your Honours, and I've handed them to the Defence already. And he's the witness, Your Honour, who will take a lengthy time, but he's really effectively the last of the major lengthy witnesses in every municipality and will cover effectively nearly all the events and the documents. After that, the -- we anticipate the witnesses will become much, much shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good. There is the other problem that you had mentioned to me last week or the week before about that particular witness, whoever, young age, supposedly witnessed a murder in a garage. What's the position: I have read -- I have gone through the response of General Talic relative to your application to have the statement admitted under 92.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the situation at present is that there are two members of the family supposed to be testifying live before this Chamber, and one Rule 92. And there was no objection to the Rule 92 witness, subject to somebody coming along to give evidence. The situation at the moment is that we are making attempts, which we don't know yet will be successful or not, to persuade them. Although we understand that they do not wish to give evidence, that in the light of things, we would wish them to give evidence. I don't know what the upshot would be, but we'll let Your Honour know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Ms. Korner. I think we can now go into closed session before we bring the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Inayat has, as Your Honour knows -- because I think you've been given copies -- done his usual stroll through the exhibits. Madam Fauveau delivered this morning -- no, yesterday, I think -- no? Monday? Tuesday? Yes. Whatever day. This morning. I've lost it now -- a letter in which she listed again the exhibits to which objection is taken to the admissibility, based on the lack of signature or stamp. The only question I have is whether Your Honour wishes me to formally put Mr. Inayat back into the witness box to confirm his schedule and then for me to apply to admit, or whether we can simply dispense with that. It's really a matter for the Trial Chamber and Defence counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau. I think we can proceed as we proceeded -- as we did last time and we dispensed from --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, we didn't, actually, Your Honour. We called him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was the first time. The second time he did, but we didn't go through the same exercise as before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. That's what I mean. It was very short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I mean -- that's what I mean. He may just come -- show up, confirm, and practically exit --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that's why I'm asking whether Your Honour wants that done. Because if so, he'll come in before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so. I think I don't even need to ask the Defence for that. I mean, it's safer. It's safer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I really don't see any use in bringing this witness once again, because the objections I have made are ones that he cannot respond to. We are not contesting that the exhibits were found where he says they were found and that they were put on the list given by the Prosecutor. What we are contesting is that those sources are not reliable sources where they were found. The places where they were found are not reliable places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So at that point, Ms. Korner, if you don't want to bring Mr. Inayat forward, you might as well decide to do that. So it's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm content, if -- clearly Madam Fauveau is content -- Mr. Ackerman hasn't troubled this time round.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. But Mr. Ackerman has never raised the issue before. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He has actually, but very early on he raised the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no. Not after it was settled -- not after Mr. Inayat was produced the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Well, in that case, Your Honour, I don't see a necessity. As I say, Judge Draganovic is going to be such a long witness we might as well get on with him. So in that case, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you just mentioned his name, and I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He's not a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's not protected. I see. Okay. Yes, you are right. He's not a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't insist on Mr. Inayat being here, Mr. Ackerman No?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I rather enjoy his presence, Your Honour, but I don't need him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, then tomorrow there are a few matters I want to move on with before we move on to Sanski Most. But I'll apply to Your Honour to formally admit the two folders as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Tomorrow the sitting will start at 1.30 here, in Courtroom III. Okay? And the Sanski Most documents, we'll have them admitted tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the schedule says Courtroom I. Is it Courtroom III?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is Courtroom III, yes. Right, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and wish you good evening, and we'll meet tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 6.30 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of April, 2002, at 1.30 p.m. 22 23 24 25
